A cell in a table.

Its value is carried as a formatted display string in `value`, a typed underlying value in `unformatted_value`, or both. It can also have a formula and per-cell style and format overrides.

fields.description: The cell's content as a pre-formatted string (for example, `$1,234.56`, `12/25/2024`, or `42%`). It's the simplest representation, intended for readers that render the cell as plain text. For the typed value, use `unformatted_value`.
fields.name: value

fields.description: The cell's typed underlying value (`number`, `text`, `date`, `boolean`, or `rich_text`), which lets a reader recover the value's type when `value` is only the formatted string. It's absent when the value has no typed form: a formula that evaluated to an error arrives with `formula` set and an empty `value`, so an absent typed value doesn't mean the cell is empty.
fields.name: unformatted_value

fields.description: The cell's value-formatting override. If it's set, it overrides the column-level default in `Table.ColumnHeader.cell_format` for this cell only.
fields.name: cell_format

fields.description: The cell's styling override (fill, alignment, padding, and wrap). If it's set, it overrides the table-, column-, and row-level defaults for this cell only.
fields.name: cell_properties

fields.name: strokes

fields.description: The IDs of the objects, such as shapes and images, that are anchored to the cell. Keynote ignores them.
fields.name: anchored_objects

fields.name: column_index

fields.name: formula

It's only meaningful for a cell whose formula spills, and it's absent when the spill is blocked. The other cells in the range hold the last spilled result and are replaced on re-evaluation. A corner ID matching no row or column of this table is ignored without a warning, and the cells it would have covered keep the values written for them.
fields.name: spill_range

fields.description: The ID of a shared conditional style set, declared in `Table.conditional_style_sets`, that applies to the cell. Keynote doesn't write `automatic`: a cell set to Automatic is written with the format its value is displayed in, such as `number` or `date_time`, and opens set to that format rather than to Automatic, unless that format is `text`.

Pie, donut, scatter, and bubble charts have no category axis. A category axis describes only its own appearance; the category names themselves come from the data grid's row or column labels, whichever `ChartData.plot_direction` leaves as the category direction.

The data used for image, movie, and audio media, and for image fills and image bullets.

Resources can be carried inline (`base64_encoded`), which makes the JSON self-contained, or refer to files stored alongside the JSON in the archive (`indirect`), which keeps large assets out of the JSON but can be read only when those files are present. What happens when bytes can't be read (an `indirect` name that matches no file, or a `base64_encoded` string that isn't valid Base64) depends on where the resource is used. An image, movie, or audio object whose media can't be read is dropped with a warning, though a `Movie.poster_image` that can't be read doesn't drop the movie. Such an object placed inline in the text of a text box or shape removes the whole text box or shape, including all of its text, and so does an image bullet in that text. An image fill in a `SlideLayout.background` removes that whole layout, and one anywhere else is left out. An image bullet or such an object in a slide's presenter notes (`Slide.note`), or an image bullet in a list style in `Presentation.stylesheet`, stops the document from loading.
